transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I just keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t be forgetting. Important stuff, you know? Like my heart follow-up appointments, or remembering to call the clinic back when they leave a message. Or I'll go to do a repair job around the house and show up without the right tools. 

Which reminds me, I was looking for my good socket wrench the other day, the old Craftsman one. They don't make 'em like that anymore, you know? Everything you buy now is cheap metal that strips the second you put some actual elbow grease into it. I got that wrench at Sears back in maybe '85. Man, I miss Sears. Used to be you could buy a washing machine, a pair of work boots, and a lawnmower all in one trip. My wife and I would go down there just about every Saturday to walk around the mall... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, just... forgetting the important things, mostly.
Did you notice these memory problems start suddenly, or have they developed slowly over time?

Well, it wasn't really a slow thing, but it wasn't overnight either. I'd say it's been causing me real trouble for about a year and two months. That was right around the time I had my cardiac scare. Scared the absolute daylights out of my wife, let me tell you. After that, the doctors made me cut way back on my walking and my garage projects—which is really the stuff that always used to keep me settled, you know? 

I used to walk all over this neighborhood. Three miles a day, easy. Down past the old elementary school, right through the park... they put in those new benches at the park, by the way. Just terrible design. They're made of that recycled plastic material that gets hotter than a frying pan in the summer. I sat on one back in July and practically burned my jeans off. I mean, who approves these things? The city council just throws money at whatever sounds good on paper, but they don't think about the practical application of it at all. My buddy Tom went to a town hall meeting to complain about it, but they wouldn't even give him the microphone. 

Anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, about a year and two months, ever since the heart thing made me stop moving around so much.
Thinking back to your childhood or school years, did you ever struggle with staying focused, being organized, or sitting still?

Oh, boy, did I ever. Even as a little kid in grade school, I was the one who just could not stay in his seat. I was always blurting out the answers before the teacher even finished asking, and I got so many notes sent home to my parents for talking too much. 

I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Higgins, she used to write those notes on this thick yellow paper. They always smelled like the mimeograph machine. You remember those? With the purple ink? Man, I loved that smell. Kids today have no idea. Everything is iPads and smartboards now. My grandson, he's nine, and he doesn't even know how to read cursive! Can you believe that? They just stopped teaching it in his district. I asked him to read a birthday card my sister sent him, and he just stared at it like it was Greek. I mean, how are these kids going to sign a check when they grow up? Or read historical documents? The Declaration of Independence is in cursive, for crying out loud. It just seems like a real shame to let a skill like that die out just because everyone wants to type on a screen... 

Wait, what was the question again? I know we were talking about school.
